title: Punishment for Murder
legal_text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
simple_explanation: If someone unlawfully kills another person with the intent to kill (or knowledge that their act is likely to cause death), it is murder, and it carries the harshest penalties in Indian criminal law.
purpose: Protects the right to life by deterring and punishing unlawful killing.
punishment: Death or imprisonment for life, and fine.
relevant_documents: FIR, post-mortem/medical report, forensic evidence, witness statements.
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Government of India. Official text is published at indiacode.nic.in; this entry was cross-verified against multiple independent legal-reference sources reproducing the bare act (apnilaw.com, lawrato.com, devgan.in, testbook.com) since the official site blocks automated fetches.
simple_explanation_te: చంపాలనే ఉద్దేశంతో (లేదా తన చర్య మరణానికి దారితీసే అవకాశం ఉందని తెలిసి) ఎవరైనా మరొక వ్యక్తిని చట్టవిరుద్ధంగా చంపితే, అది హత్య అవుతుంది, మరియు భారత క్రిమినల్ చట్టంలో ఇది అత్యంత కఠినమైన శిక్షలను కలిగి ఉంటుంది.
purpose_te: చట్టవిరుద్ధమైన హత్యను నిరోధించడం మరియు శిక్షించడం ద్వారా జీవించే హక్కును రక్షిస్తుంది.
punishment_te: మరణశిక్ష లేదా జీవిత ఖైదు, మరియు జరిమానా కూడా విధించవచ్చు.
relevant_documents_te: FIR, పోస్ట్‌మార్టం/వైద్య నివేదిక, ఫోరెన్సిక్ ఆధారాలు, సాక్షుల వాంగ్మూలాలు.

title: Cheating
legal_text: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to cheat. A dishonest concealment of facts is a deception within the meaning of this section.
simple_explanation: Tricking or deceiving someone into handing over property, money, or a document, or into doing/not doing something that harms them, counts as cheating. Sub-section 318(4) — dishonestly inducing delivery of property — is the direct successor to the old 'Section 420' cheating offence.
purpose: Protects individuals and businesses from fraud and deception.
punishment: Graded by sub-section: general cheating (318(2)) — up to 3 years, or fine, or both. Cheating breaching a duty to protect the victim's interests (318(3)) — up to 5 years, or fine, or both. Cheating that induces delivery of property or alters a valuable security (318(4), the old 'Section 420' offence) — up to 7 years AND fine (mandatory at this tier).
relevant_documents: Bank statement highlighting fraudulent transactions, agreements/receipts/invoices, screenshots of chats, police complaint copy.
key_elements:
Deception of any person.
Fraudulent or dishonest inducement to deliver property or make payments.
Intentional inducement causing damage or harm to the person deceived.
relevant_information:
Communication records (messages, emails, call logs).
Bank transfer receipts, UPI transaction IDs, cheque copies.
Promises made in writing or verbally.
keywords: cheating, fraud, scam, deception, fake, duped, 420, money fraud, bns 318
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 318. Cross-verified against lawrato.com, apnilaw.com, drishtijudiciary.com, and ezylegal.in. Note: the section's heading is 'Cheating' generally; 'inducing delivery of property' specifically describes sub-section (4).
simple_explanation_te: ఎవరైనా ఆస్తి, డబ్బు లేదా పత్రాన్ని అప్పగించేలా, లేదా వారికి హాని కలిగించే పనిని చేసేలా/చేయకుండా ఉండేలా మోసం చేసి లేదా వంచించి ప్రేరేపించడం మోసంగా పరిగణించబడుతుంది. ఉపవిభాగం 318(4) — ఆస్తిని అప్పగించేలా నిజాయితీ లేకుండా ప్రేరేపించడం — పాత 'సెక్షన్ 420' మోసం నేరానికి నేరుగా వారసత్వం.
purpose_te: వ్యక్తులను మరియు వ్యాపారాలను మోసం మరియు వంచన నుండి రక్షిస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఉపవిభాగాన్ని బట్టి తీవ్రత మారుతుంది: సాధారణ మోసం (318(2)) — 3 సంవత్సరాల వరకు, లేదా జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ. బాధితుడి ప్రయోజనాలను రక్షించే బాధ్యతను ఉల్లంఘించే మోసం (318(3)) — 5 సంవత్సరాల వరకు, లేదా జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ. ఆస్తి అప్పగింతకు లేదా విలువైన సెక్యూరిటీ మార్పుకు దారితీసే మోసం (318(4), పాత 'సెక్షన్ 420' నేరం) — 7 సంవత్సరాల వరకు మరియు జరిమానా (ఈ స్థాయిలో తప్పనిసరి).
key_elements_te:
ఏదైనా వ్యక్తిని మోసగించడం.
ఆస్తిని అప్పగించేలా లేదా చెల్లింపులు చేసేలా మోసపూరితంగా లేదా నిజాయితీ లేకుండా ప్రేరేపించడం.
మోసగించబడిన వ్యక్తికి హాని కలిగించే ఉద్దేశపూర్వక ప్రేరేపణ.
relevant_information_te:
కమ్యూనికేషన్ రికార్డులు (సందేశాలు, ఇమెయిల్‌లు, కాల్ లాగ్‌లు).
బ్యాంక్ బదిలీ రసీదులు, UPI లావాదేవీ IDలు, చెక్కు కాపీలు.
వ్రాతపూర్వకంగా లేదా మౌఖికంగా ఇచ్చిన వాగ్దానాలు.
relevant_documents_te: మోసపూరిత లావాదేవీలను చూపే బ్యాంక్ స్టేట్‌మెంట్, ఒప్పందాలు/రసీదులు/ఇన్వాయిస్‌లు, చాట్‌ల స్క్రీన్‌షాట్‌లు, పోలీసు ఫిర్యాదు కాపీ.

title: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty
legal_text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
simple_explanation: Every person — citizen or not — has the fundamental right not to be deprived of life or personal liberty, except through a fair legal process. Courts have interpreted this broadly to include rights to dignity, privacy, livelihood, a clean environment, and health.
purpose: Guarantees the fundamental right to life and personal liberty against arbitrary state action.
punishment: Not a penal provision — remedies are constitutional, via a writ petition under Article 32 (Supreme Court) or Article 226 (High Court).
relevant_documents: Writ petition, evidence of the rights violation.
source: The Constitution of India, Part III (Fundamental Rights). Official text is published at indiacode.nic.in / legislative.gov.in; cross-verified against multiple independent legal-reference sources.
title_te: జీవించే మరియు వ్యక్తిగత స్వేచ్ఛ హక్కు రక్షణ
simple_explanation_te: ప్రతి వ్యక్తికి — పౌరుడైనా కాకపోయినా — చట్టం నిర్దేశించిన సక్రమమైన ప్రక్రియ ద్వారా తప్ప, జీవితం లేదా వ్యక్తిగత స్వేచ్ఛను కోల్పోకుండా ఉండే ప్రాథమిక హక్కు ఉంది. గౌరవం, గోప్యత, జీవనోపాధి, పరిశుభ్రమైన పర్యావరణం మరియు ఆరోగ్యం వంటి హక్కులను కూడా ఇందులో భాగంగా న్యాయస్థానాలు విస్తృతంగా వ్యాఖ్యానించాయి.
purpose_te: ఏకపక్ష రాజ్య చర్యకు వ్యతిరేకంగా జీవించే మరియు వ్యక్తిగత స్వేచ్ఛ హక్కుకు హామీ ఇస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — పరిష్కారాలు రాజ్యాంగపరమైనవి, ఆర్టికల్ 32 (సుప్రీంకోర్టు) లేదా ఆర్టికల్ 226 (హైకోర్టు) కింద రిట్ పిటిషన్ ద్వారా.
relevant_documents_te: రిట్ పిటిషన్, హక్కుల ఉల్లంఘనకు సంబంధించిన ఆధారాలు.

title: Person Arrested to be Informed of Grounds of Arrest and of Right to Bail
legal_text: Every police officer or other person arresting any person without warrant shall forthwith communicate to him full particulars of the offence for which he is arrested or other grounds for such arrest. Where a police officer arrests without warrant any person other than a person accused of a non-bailable offence, he shall inform the person arrested that he is entitled to be released on bail and that he may arrange for sureties.
simple_explanation: If you're arrested, the police must immediately tell you why you're being arrested — and if it's for a bailable offence, they must tell you you're entitled to bail.
purpose: Prevents arbitrary arrest by requiring the reason to be stated immediately, upholding Article 22.
punishment: Not a penal provision — a procedural safeguard; non-compliance can render an arrest illegal and support release via habeas corpus.
relevant_documents: Arrest memo stating the grounds, bail application, surety identification documents.
key_elements:
Immediate communication of specific allegations and section numbers.
Information regarding the bailable nature of the alleged offence (for bailable offences only).
Right to arrange sureties if the offence is bailable.
relevant_information:
Whether the offence is classified as bailable or non-bailable.
Name and badge number of the arresting officer.
keywords: arrested, bail, rights, grounds, police custody, lawyer, bnss 47
source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, Section 47. Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org, apnilaw.com, latestlaws.com, sanhita.ai, and truelawyer.in.
title_te: అరెస్టు కారణాలు మరియు జామీను హక్కు గురించి తెలియజేయాలి
simple_explanation_te: మిమ్మల్ని అరెస్టు చేస్తే, మిమ్మల్ని ఎందుకు అరెస్టు చేస్తున్నారో పోలీసులు వెంటనే తెలియజేయాలి — మరియు అది జామీను పొందగల నేరం అయితే, మీకు జామీను హక్కు ఉందని కూడా వారు తెలియజేయాలి.
purpose_te: ఆర్టికల్ 22ను సమర్థిస్తూ, కారణాన్ని వెంటనే తెలియజేయాలని కోరడం ద్వారా ఏకపక్ష అరెస్టును నిరోధిస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — విధానపరమైన రక్షణ; దీన్ని పాటించకపోతే అరెస్టు చట్టవిరుద్ధమైనదిగా పరిగణించి, హేబియస్ కార్పస్ ద్వారా విడుదలకు దారితీయవచ్చు.
key_elements_te:
ఆరోపణలు మరియు సెక్షన్ నంబర్లతో సహా వెంటనే తెలియజేయాలి.
నేరం జామీను పొందదగినదా కాదా అనే సమాచారం (జామీను పొందదగిన నేరాలకు మాత్రమే).
నేరం జామీను పొందదగినది అయితే ష్యూరిటీలు ఏర్పాటు చేసుకునే హక్కు.
relevant_information_te:
నేరం జామీను పొందదగినదా, కాదా అనేది.
అరెస్టు చేసిన అధికారి పేరు మరియు బ్యాడ్జ్ నంబర్.
relevant_documents_te: కారణాలను తెలిపే అరెస్టు మెమో, జామీను దరఖాస్తు, ష్యూరిటీ గుర్తింపు పత్రాలు.

title: Right to Inform a Relative or Friend of the Arrest
legal_text: The police officer or person making the arrest shall forthwith give information regarding the arrest and the place where the arrested person is being held, to a relative, friend, or other person nominated by the arrested person for that purpose.
simple_explanation: You have the right to have the police tell someone you choose — a relative or friend — that you've been arrested and where you're being held.
purpose: Ensures the arrested person is not held incommunicado.
punishment: Not a penal provision — a procedural safeguard for the arrested person.
relevant_documents: Arrest memo naming the informed person.
source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023), Government of India — replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 from 1 July 2024. Official text is published at indiacode.nic.in; this entry was cross-verified against multiple independent legal-reference sources (indiankanoon.org, apnilaw.com, drishtijudiciary.com, latestlaws.com) since the official site blocks automated fetches.
title_te: బంధువుకు లేదా స్నేహితుడికి అరెస్టు గురించి తెలియజేసే హక్కు
simple_explanation_te: మిమ్మల్ని అరెస్టు చేశారని, మిమ్మల్ని ఎక్కడ ఉంచారని మీరు ఎంచుకున్న బంధువుకు లేదా స్నేహితుడికి పోలీసులు తెలియజేయాలని మీకు హక్కు ఉంది.
purpose_te: అరెస్టు చేసిన వ్యక్తిని బయటి ప్రపంచంతో సంబంధం లేకుండా ఉంచకుండా చూస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — అరెస్టు చేసిన వ్యక్తి కోసం విధానపరమైన రక్షణ.
relevant_documents_te: తెలియజేయబడిన వ్యక్తి పేరుతో ఉన్న అరెస్టు మెమో.

title: Restriction on Arrest of Women After Sunset
legal_text: As a general rule, no woman shall be arrested after sunset and before sunrise. Where exceptional circumstances exist, a woman police officer must obtain prior written permission of a Magistrate of the First Class within whose local jurisdiction the offence is committed or the arrest is to be made.
simple_explanation: Ordinarily, a woman cannot be arrested at night. If there's an exceptional reason to do so, it must be a woman police officer making the arrest, with a magistrate's prior written permission.
purpose: Protects women from arrest procedures at night absent exceptional justification.
punishment: Not a penal provision — a procedural safeguard for women being arrested.
relevant_documents: Magistrate's written permission (in exceptional cases).
source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023), Government of India — replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 from 1 July 2024. Official text is published at indiacode.nic.in; this entry was cross-verified against multiple independent legal-reference sources (indiankanoon.org, apnilaw.com, drishtijudiciary.com, latestlaws.com) since the official site blocks automated fetches.
title_te: సూర్యాస్తమయం తర్వాత మహిళలను అరెస్టు చేయడంపై పరిమితి
simple_explanation_te: సాధారణంగా, రాత్రి సమయంలో ఒక మహిళను అరెస్టు చేయకూడదు. అసాధారణ కారణం ఉంటే, అరెస్టు చేసేది మహిళా పోలీసు అధికారి అయి ఉండాలి మరియు మేజిస్ట్రేట్ ముందస్తు వ్రాతపూర్వక అనుమతి తప్పనిసరి.
purpose_te: అసాధారణ కారణం లేకుండా రాత్రిపూట అరెస్టు విధానాల నుండి మహిళలను రక్షిస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — అరెస్టు చేయబడుతున్న మహిళల కోసం విధానపరమైన రక్షణ.

title: Production Before a Magistrate Within 24 Hours
legal_text: No police officer shall detain a person arrested without a warrant in custody for a period longer than is reasonable, and such period shall not exceed twenty-four hours, excluding the time necessary for travel from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's court, without a special order of a Magistrate. Every arrested person shall be produced before the nearest Magistrate within that 24-hour period.
simple_explanation: The police can't hold you for more than 24 hours (not counting travel time to court) without a magistrate's order — you must be produced before a magistrate within that time.
purpose: Prevents indefinite detention without judicial oversight.
punishment: Not a penal provision — a procedural safeguard for the arrested person.
relevant_documents: Remand order, production record.
source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023), Government of India — replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 from 1 July 2024. Official text is published at indiacode.nic.in; this entry was cross-verified against multiple independent legal-reference sources (indiankanoon.org, apnilaw.com, drishtijudiciary.com, latestlaws.com) since the official site blocks automated fetches.
simple_explanation_te: మేజిస్ట్రేట్ ఉత్తర్వు లేకుండా పోలీసులు మిమ్మల్ని 24 గంటల కంటే ఎక్కువసేపు (కోర్టుకు ప్రయాణించే సమయం మినహాయించి) నిర్బంధంలో ఉంచలేరు — ఆ సమయంలోపు మిమ్మల్ని సమీప మేజిస్ట్రేట్ ముందు హాజరుపరచాలి.
purpose_te: న్యాయపరమైన పర్యవేక్షణ లేకుండా అనిశ్చిత నిర్బంధాన్ని నివారిస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — అరెస్టు చేయబడిన వ్యక్తి కోసం విధానపరమైన రక్షణ.

title: Right to Consult and Be Defended by a Legal Practitioner
legal_text: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice.
simple_explanation: You have the constitutional right to consult a lawyer of your choice and be defended by them. If you can't afford one, the Supreme Court (Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar, 1980) held the state must provide free legal aid — see the Legal Help section of this app for the NALSA helpline.
purpose: Guarantees access to legal representation as a fundamental right.
punishment: Not a penal provision — a fundamental constitutional right.
relevant_documents: None required to exercise this right.
source: The Constitution of India, Part III (Fundamental Rights). Official text is published at indiacode.nic.in / legislative.gov.in; cross-verified against multiple independent legal-reference sources.
simple_explanation_te: మీకు నచ్చిన న్యాయవాదిని సంప్రదించి, ఆయన/ఆమె ద్వారా రక్షణ పొందే రాజ్యాంగ హక్కు మీకు ఉంది. మీరు భరించలేకపోతే, రాష్ట్రం ఉచిత న్యాయ సహాయం అందించాలని సుప్రీంకోర్టు (హుస్సేనారా ఖాతూన్ వర్సెస్ బీహార్ రాష్ట్రం, 1980) తీర్పు ఇచ్చింది — ఈ యాప్‌లోని లీగల్ హెల్ప్ విభాగంలో NALSA హెల్ప్‌లైన్ చూడండి.
purpose_te: న్యాయ ప్రాతినిధ్యానికి ప్రాథమిక హక్కుగా హామీ ఇస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — ఇది ఒక ప్రాథమిక రాజ్యాంగ హక్కు.
relevant_documents_te: ఈ హక్కును వినియోగించుకోవడానికి ఎలాంటి పత్రాలు అవసరం లేదు.

title: Theft
legal_text: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
simple_explanation: Taking someone else's movable property without their permission, intending to keep it dishonestly, is theft — for example, a phone, vehicle, or cash taken without consent.
purpose: Protects personal property from being dishonestly taken by others.
punishment: First conviction: imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both. Second or subsequent conviction: rigorous imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, with fine. For first-time theft of property under Rs. 5,000, with the property returned/restored, community service may apply instead.
relevant_documents: FIR / police complaint, proof of ownership/possession, police seizure memo, IMEI/serial number documentation.
key_elements:
The property must be movable (phone, vehicle, jewellery, cash).
The property was in the possession of another person.
The taking was done dishonestly, without the owner's consent.
The property was moved in order to take it.
relevant_information:
Exact date, time, and location where the property was last seen.
Proof of ownership (invoice, IMEI number, registration certificate).
Whether the item was locked, in a vehicle, or in a public space.
keywords: theft, stole, phone, stealing, laptop, wallet, property, dishonest, bns 303
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 303. Cross-verified against ipleaders.in, apnilaw.com, testbook.com, and lawrato.com (official indiacode.nic.in blocks automated fetches).
simple_explanation_te: ఒక వ్యక్తి అనుమతి లేకుండా, నిజాయితీ లేకుండా ఉంచుకోవాలనే ఉద్దేశ్యంతో మరొకరి కదిలే ఆస్తిని తీసుకోవడం దొంగతనం — ఉదాహరణకు, అనుమతి లేకుండా తీసుకున్న ఫోన్, వాహనం లేదా నగదు.
purpose_te: ఇతరులు నిజాయితీ లేకుండా తీసుకెళ్లకుండా వ్యక్తిగత ఆస్తిని రక్షిస్తుంది.
punishment_te: మొదటి నేరారోపణ: 3 సంవత్సరాల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, లేదా జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ. రెండవ లేదా తదుపరి నేరారోపణ: 1 నుండి 5 సంవత్సరాల కఠిన కారాగార శిక్ష, జరిమానాతో సహా. రూ. 5,000 లోపు విలువైన ఆస్తికి మొదటిసారి దొంగతనం జరిగి, ఆస్తిని తిరిగి ఇచ్చినట్లయితే, జైలుకు బదులుగా సామాజిక సేవ విధించవచ్చు.
key_elements_te:
ఆస్తి కదిలేదిగా ఉండాలి (ఫోన్, వాహనం, నగలు, నగదు).
ఆస్తి మరొక వ్యక్తి స్వాధీనంలో ఉండాలి.
యజమాని అనుమతి లేకుండా నిజాయితీ లేకుండా తీసుకున్నారు.
తీసుకోవడానికి ఆస్తిని కదిలించారు.
relevant_information_te:
ఆస్తి చివరిగా కనిపించిన ఖచ్చితమైన తేదీ, సమయం, స్థలం.
యాజమాన్య రుజువు (ఇన్వాయిస్, IMEI నంబర్, రిజిస్ట్రేషన్ సర్టిఫికేట్).
వస్తువు లాక్ చేయబడిందా, వాహనంలో ఉందా, బహిరంగ ప్రదేశంలో ఉందా.
relevant_documents_te: FIR / పోలీసు ఫిర్యాదు, యాజమాన్యం/స్వాధీన రుజువు, పోలీసు స్వాధీన మెమో, IMEI/సీరియల్ నంబర్ డాక్యుమెంటేషన్.

title: Snatching
legal_text: Theft is 'snatching' if, in order to commit theft, the offender suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizes or secures or grabs or takes away from any person or from his possession any movable property.
simple_explanation: When someone suddenly grabs your phone or chain from your hand or neck and runs away, it is classified as snatching — a distinct, standalone offence with no direct IPC equivalent.
purpose: Provides a distinct legal provision addressing street crimes involving sudden, forcible grabbing of valuables.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and the offender shall also be liable to fine.
relevant_documents: FIR copy, medical examination report if injury occurred, invoice showing ownership of the snatched item.
key_elements:
Commission of theft by sudden seizure or grabbing.
Property was held or worn by the person.
Sudden force or speed used to dispossess the owner.
relevant_information:
Exact spot of occurrence and route taken by the accused.
Vehicle description if a bike/scooter was used.
Any physical injury sustained during the snatching.
keywords: snatching, chain snatching, phone snatching, grabbed, street crime, bns 304
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 304. Cross-verified against devgan.in, lawrato.com, vakilsearch.com, and apnilaw.com.

title: Robbery
legal_text: In all robbery there is either theft or extortion. Theft is robbery if, in order to the committing of the theft, or in committing the theft, or in carrying away property obtained by the theft, the offender voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death, instant hurt, or instant wrongful restraint.
simple_explanation: If someone steals from you by threatening you, hurting you, or putting you in fear of physical harm, the offence escalates from simple theft to robbery.
purpose: Penalizes the violent element introduced during an unauthorized taking of property.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment for a term up to 10 years, and fine; if committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, up to 14 years. Attempted robbery: up to 7 years rigorous imprisonment and fine. Robbery causing hurt: imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
relevant_documents: FIR mentioning weapons/threats used, medico-legal case (MLC) report, witness statements.
key_elements:
Theft or extortion was being committed.
Offender caused, or attempted to cause, hurt, death, or wrongful restraint.
Action created immediate fear of physical harm.
relevant_information:
Nature of any weapon or threat used.
Number of persons involved.
Physical injuries caused to victim or bystanders.
keywords: robbery, threat, weapon, force, extortion, dacoity, bns 309
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 309. Cross-verified against lawrato.com, testbook.com, and vakilsearch.com.

title: Criminal Breach of Trust
legal_text: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law or of any legal contract which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, commits criminal breach of trust.
simple_explanation: If you give your car, money, or goods to someone you trusted (an employee, partner, or custodian) for safekeeping, and they use it for their own gain without your permission, that is a criminal breach of trust.
purpose: Holds custodians, fiduciaries, and trustees accountable for entrusted property.
punishment: General offence: imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both. Aggravated categories (carriers, warehouse-keepers, clerks/servants): up to 7 years and fine. By a public servant, banker, merchant, or agent: imprisonment for life or up to 10 years, and fine.
relevant_documents: Agreement/contract, receipts showing transfer of custody, legal notice demanding restitution, bank records.
key_elements:
Entrustment of property to the accused.
Dishonest misappropriation or conversion to their own use.
Violation of a legal direction or agreement governing the trust.
relevant_information:
Proof of entrustment (handover receipt, contract, partnership deed).
Demand notice requesting return of the property.
Refusal or evasive response from the accused.
keywords: breach of trust, entrusted, misappropriation, partner, agent, deposit, bns 316
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 316. Cross-verified against devgan.in and lawrato.com.

title: Criminal Intimidation
legal_text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do, as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat, commits criminal intimidation.
simple_explanation: When someone threatens to beat you up, ruin your reputation, damage your property, or harm your family to scare you or force you to act against your will.
purpose: Protects individual mental peace, liberty, and physical safety against threats.
punishment: Basic threats: imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both. Threats of death, grievous hurt, destruction of property by fire, or imputing unchastity to a woman (aggravated): up to 7 years, or fine, or both. A further 2 years may be added if the threat was made anonymously.
relevant_documents: Audio/video evidence of the threats, exported chat logs with metadata, FIR copy.
key_elements:
Threat of injury to person, reputation, or property.
Intent to cause alarm or force the person to act against their will.
relevant_information:
Audio recordings, text messages, or letters containing threats.
Details of any prior dispute or context.
Eyewitnesses present during the incident.
keywords: threat, intimidation, blackmail, danger, harm, warning, bns 351
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 351. Cross-verified against testbook.com, lawrato.com, vakilsearch.com, and righttolaw.com.

title: Voluntarily Causing Hurt
legal_text: Whoever does any act with the intention of thereby causing hurt to any person, or with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause hurt to any person, and does thereby cause hurt to any person, is said to 'voluntarily cause hurt'.
simple_explanation: When someone intentionally punches, slaps, kicks, or physically hits you and causes bodily pain or injury, it is treated as voluntarily causing hurt.
purpose: Protects bodily integrity and penalizes physical violence.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 10,000, or both.
relevant_documents: Medico-legal case (MLC) report, doctor's prescription/treatment bill, photographs of injuries, FIR.
key_elements:
Bodily pain, disease, or infirmity caused.
Intention to cause hurt, or knowledge that the act is likely to cause hurt.
relevant_information:
Time and place of the assault.
Names of witnesses present.
Whether weapons or objects were used (which may elevate the offence).
keywords: assault, hurt, beaten, injury, fight, physical violence, bns 115
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 115. Cross-verified against lawrato.com, vidhijudicial.com, testbook.com, and apnilaw.com.

title: Defamation
legal_text: Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said to defame that person.
simple_explanation: When someone publicly spreads false, harmful statements or posts about you, knowing it will damage your reputation.
purpose: Safeguards an individual's dignity, social standing, and reputation.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both, or community service. The offence is non-cognizable and bailable, generally triable by a Magistrate of the first class.
relevant_documents: Screenshots of posts with URLs/timestamps, legal notice demanding retraction, witness affidavits.
key_elements:
Making or publishing an imputation.
The imputation concerns the aggrieved person.
Intention or knowledge that it will harm reputation.
Does not fall under a recognized legal exception (e.g. truth for public good).
relevant_information:
Exact words, audio, video, or publication used.
Proof that the publication reached third parties.
Evidence disproving the false claims.
keywords: defamation, reputation, slander, libel, false claim, social media post, bns 356
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 356. Cross-verified against devgan.in, lawrato.com, testbook.com, and vakilsearch.com.

title: Assault or Criminal Force to Woman with Intent to Outrage her Modesty
legal_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
simple_explanation: Protects women from unwanted physical touch, aggressive advances, or physical assault aimed at violating personal dignity — the direct successor to old IPC Section 354.
purpose: Enforces zero tolerance for gender-based violence and protects women's dignity and safety.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description, not less than 1 year and up to 5 years, and fine. Cognizable and non-bailable.
relevant_documents: FIR / Zero FIR, statement before a Magistrate, medical examination report if force was used, digital evidence.
key_elements:
Assault or use of criminal force against a woman.
Intention to outrage her modesty, or knowledge that it is likely to do so.
relevant_information:
Precise location, time, and sequence of events.
Eyewitnesses or CCTV coverage.
Identity of the perpetrator (known person, colleague, stranger).
keywords: women safety, molestation, outrage modesty, harassment, stalking, bns 74
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 74. Cross-verified against devgan.in, writinglaw.com, vakilsearch.com, testbook.com, and lawrato.com.

title: Cheating by Personation by Using Computer Resource
legal_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
simple_explanation: If someone creates a fake identity online (pretending to be a bank official, army officer, or friend) over a call, message, or website to trick you into transferring money or sharing your OTP/credentials, this is the applicable offence.
purpose: Combats digital impersonation, phishing attacks, and online financial fraud.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 3 years, and fine up to Rs. 1,00,000.
relevant_documents: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal complaint receipt, bank statement, screenshots of SMS/OTP requests and chats.
key_elements:
Use of a computer resource or communication device.
Deception by pretending to be someone else.
Cheating and dishonest inducement.
relevant_information:
Transaction ID, UTR number, beneficiary account details.
Phone numbers, emails, or website links used by the fraudster.
Acknowledgement number from cybercrime.gov.in (Helpline 1930).
keywords: cyber fraud, online scam, phishing, fake profile, otp fraud, impersonation, it act 66d
source: Information Technology Act, 2000, Section 66D. Cross-verified against apnilaw.com, sanhita.ai, kanoongpt.in, and worldlawdigest.com.

title: Punishment for Identity Theft
legal_text: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh.
simple_explanation: If someone steals your email password, social media login, UPI PIN, or digital signature and uses it without your permission, they can be prosecuted under this section.
purpose: Safeguards digital identities, passwords, and electronic credentials.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 3 years, and fine up to Rs. 1,00,000.
relevant_documents: Security alert emails, screenshots of unauthorized account changes, cyber police complaint copy.
key_elements:
Unauthorized use of electronic signature, password, or biometric data.
Done dishonestly or fraudulently.
relevant_information:
Access logs and login-alert emails from service providers.
IP address / device information in security logs, if available.
Services accessed without authorization.
keywords: identity theft, password, digital signature, biometric, hacked, stolen credentials, it act 66c
source: Information Technology Act, 2000, Section 66C. Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org, apnilaw.com, and worldlawdigest.com.

title: When Police May Arrest Without Warrant
legal_text: A police officer may arrest a person without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant where a cognizable offence is committed in their presence, or on credible information/reasonable suspicion. For offences punishable with less than seven years' imprisonment, the officer must additionally believe arrest is necessary for a specified purpose (preventing further offence, ensuring proper investigation, preventing evidence tampering, etc.) and must record reasons in writing — both when making, and when choosing not to make, the arrest.
simple_explanation: Explains when police can arrest someone without a magistrate's warrant. For offences carrying under 7 years, arrest is meant to be the exception: the officer must normally issue a notice to appear instead, unless there's a specific, recorded reason arrest is necessary.
purpose: Balances law-enforcement power with constitutional rights against arbitrary detention.
punishment: Not a penal provision — a procedural safeguard governing when and how police may arrest.
relevant_documents: Copy of arrest memo, copy of FIR/complaint, intimation memo sent to family/nominated person.
key_elements:
Cognizable offence committed in the presence of the police officer.
Reasonable complaint or credible information for offences with prescribed punishments.
For offences under 7 years: a notice of appearance is ordinarily issued instead of arrest.
Mandatory recording of reasons in writing, whether or not an arrest is made.
relevant_information:
Did the officer inform the arrested person of the exact grounds of arrest?
Was an arrest memo prepared with date, time, and witness signature?
Was a family member or friend informed immediately?
keywords: arrest, police, custody, warrant, grounds of arrest, rights, bnss 35
source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, Section 35. Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org, drishtijudiciary.com, leadindia.law, and vaishlaw.com.
title_te: వారెంట్ లేకుండా పోలీసులు ఎప్పుడు అరెస్టు చేయవచ్చు
simple_explanation_te: మేజిస్ట్రేట్ వారెంట్ లేకుండా పోలీసులు ఎప్పుడు ఒక వ్యక్తిని అరెస్టు చేయవచ్చో ఇది వివరిస్తుంది. 7 సంవత్సరాల కంటే తక్కువ శిక్ష ఉన్న నేరాలకు, అరెస్టు మినహాయింపుగా ఉండాలి: నిర్దిష్టమైన, రికార్డు చేయబడిన కారణం లేకపోతే, అధికారి సాధారణంగా అరెస్టుకు బదులుగా హాజరు నోటీసు జారీ చేయాలి.
purpose_te: ఏకపక్ష నిర్బంధానికి వ్యతిరేకంగా రాజ్యాంగ హక్కులతో చట్ట అమలు అధికారాన్ని సమతుల్యం చేస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — అరెస్టు ఎప్పుడు, ఎలా చేయాలో నియంత్రించే విధానపరమైన రక్షణ.
key_elements_te:

title: Driving by a Drunken Person or by a Person Under the Influence of Drugs
legal_text: Whoever, while driving, or attempting to drive, a motor vehicle has, in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected in a test by a breath analyser, or is under the influence of a drug to such an extent as to be incapable of exercising proper control over the vehicle, shall be punishable.
simple_explanation: Driving any vehicle after drinking alcohol, if a breathalyzer shows alcohol above the legal limit (30mg per 100ml), is an offence punishable with fines and possible jail.
purpose: Prevents road fatalities and discourages driving under substance influence.
punishment: First offence: imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 10,000, or both. Second or subsequent offence within 3 years: imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to Rs. 15,000, or both (figures as increased by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, effective 1 September 2019).
relevant_documents: E-challan copy, driving license and RC, breathalyzer test reading, vehicle insurance policy.
key_elements:
Driving or attempting to drive a motor vehicle in a public place.
Blood alcohol content exceeding 30 mg/100 ml, or incapable of proper control due to drugs.
relevant_information:
Breath analyser test slip / reading.
Blood sample testing report, if taken.
Challan / impound memo issued by traffic police.
keywords: drunk driving, alcohol, traffic, breathalyzer, fine, driving license, accident, mv act 185
source: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, as amended by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (in force from 1 September 2019). Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org and vakilsearch.com; one outdated secondary source with pre-2019 fine amounts was identified and excluded.

title: Manner in Which Complaint Shall Be Made
legal_text: A complaint may be filed before the District Commission by the consumer to whom the goods/services were sold or provided, or who alleges an unfair trade practice; by a recognized consumer association; by one or more consumers, with the Commission's permission, where numerous consumers have the same interest; or by the Central Government, Central Authority, or a State Government.
simple_explanation: If a company sold you a defective product, refused a rightful refund, or gave poor service, this section explains who can file a case in the District Consumer Commission and how — including electronic filing.
purpose: Provides an accessible mechanism for consumers to seek redress against sellers and service providers.
punishment: Not a penal provision — a procedural provision governing who may file a complaint and how.
relevant_documents: Tax invoice, warranty card copy, written communication with seller, legal notice sent (if any).
key_elements:
Complainant must be a 'consumer' (bought for consideration, not commercial resale).
Defect in goods, deficiency in service, or unfair trade practice.
Complaint (and fee payment) may be filed electronically, per prescribed rules.
relevant_information:
Invoice number, purchase date, and payment proof.
Warranty/guarantee card details.
Customer care complaints, email exchanges, and ticket numbers.
keywords: consumer, defective product, refund, warranty, consumer court, e-commerce fraud, cpa 35
source: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Government of India (Chapter IV provisions in force from 20 July 2020). Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org, ibclaw.in, and consumerprotection.in.

title: Grounds for Divorce
legal_text: Either spouse may petition for divorce on grounds including adultery, cruelty, desertion for two or more continuous years, conversion to another religion, unsoundness of mind, communicable venereal disease, renunciation of the world, or not being heard of as alive for seven years. A wife has additional exclusive grounds, including the husband's bigamy, rape, sodomy, or bestiality.
simple_explanation: Lets a husband or wife apply to court for divorce on specific grounds like cruelty, desertion, or adultery. Divorce can also be obtained by mutual consent under a separate provision (Section 13B) without needing to prove fault.
purpose: Provides a legal way to end a broken marriage, balancing marital stability with protection from abuse or injustice.
punishment: Not a penal provision — the remedy is a court decree dissolving the marriage.
relevant_documents: Marriage certificate, divorce petition, evidence supporting the ground claimed (medical records, communication records, witness statements).
key_elements:
Petitioner must be the aggrieved husband or wife.
A specific statutory ground must be proved with evidence.
Desertion must be for a continuous period of two years or more.
A wife has additional exclusive grounds beyond those available to a husband.
relevant_information:
Marriage certificate or proof of a valid Hindu marriage.
Dates and evidence supporting the specific ground claimed.
Whether mutual consent divorce (faster, no-fault) is a realistic option instead.
keywords: divorce, separation, marriage breakdown, cruelty, desertion, adultery, hindu marriage act, section 13
source: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, Section 13 (as amended by the Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976). Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org and lawbhoomi.com.

law_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Application to Magistrate for Protection and Other Orders
legal_text: An aggrieved person, a Protection Officer, or another person on her behalf may apply to the Magistrate for one or more reliefs under the Act. The Magistrate must consider any Domestic Incident Report before deciding, must ordinarily hold the first hearing within three days of the application being filed, and should endeavour to dispose of the application within sixty days of the first hearing.
simple_explanation: Lets a woman facing domestic violence go directly to a Magistrate for protection, residence, monetary relief, custody, or compensation orders — a fast civil remedy separate from filing a criminal case.
purpose: Creates an accessible, time-bound civil remedy against domestic violence, independent of criminal prosecution.
punishment: Not a penal provision — the Magistrate can pass protection, residence, monetary relief, custody, and compensation orders under related sections of the Act.
relevant_documents: Domestic Incident Report, application under Section 12, medical/police records of incidents, proof of shared household or marriage.
key_elements:
Applicant must be an 'aggrieved person' in a domestic relationship facing violence.
Application can be filed by her, a Protection Officer, or someone on her behalf.
Magistrate considers the Domestic Incident Report before deciding.
First hearing is meant to be held within 3 days; disposal targeted within 60 days.
relevant_information:
Proof of the domestic relationship (marriage certificate, shared household proof).
A documented timeline of incidents — photos, medical records, messages, police reports.
Whether a Domestic Incident Report has already been filed with a Protection Officer.
keywords: domestic violence, protection order, magistrate application, dv act, section 12, abuse complaint
source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Section 12. Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org and advocategandhi.com.

title: Order for Maintenance of Wives, Children and Parents
legal_text: A Magistrate of the First Class may order a person of sufficient means who neglects or refuses to maintain his wife (including a divorced, unremarried wife), minor children, major children with a disability, or an indigent parent, to pay a monthly allowance. Non-payment can lead to a warrant for the amount as a fine, and imprisonment of up to one month per default, subject to a one-year limit on claiming arrears.
simple_explanation: Lets a wife, child, or parent who cannot support themselves claim monthly maintenance from a person of sufficient means who is neglecting to support them — a fast, religion-neutral remedy that replaced the old CrPC Section 125.
purpose: Prevents destitution of dependents by providing a quick, summary remedy for maintenance.
punishment: Not a penal provision for the underlying conduct — but non-payment of an ordered maintenance amount can lead to a fine (recovered like a warrant) and imprisonment of up to one month per default.
relevant_documents: Marriage/birth certificates, income proof of both parties, any prior maintenance order, application for maintenance.
key_elements:
Applicant's inability to maintain themselves.
Respondent's sufficient means to pay.
Neglect or refusal by the respondent to maintain the applicant.
Relationship (wife, child, or parent) must be established.
A wife's claim can be barred by disqualifying conduct such as living in adultery.
relevant_information:
Proof of relationship — marriage certificate, birth certificates.
Evidence of the applicant's income/inability to self-support.
Evidence of the respondent's income and assets.
Any prior maintenance order (e.g. under the Hindu Marriage Act or DV Act) to avoid double claims.
keywords: maintenance, alimony, wife maintenance, child maintenance, parents maintenance, bnss 144, section 125
source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023), Government of India — replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 from 1 July 2024. Official text is published at indiacode.nic.in; this entry was cross-verified against multiple independent legal-reference sources (indiankanoon.org, apnilaw.com, drishtijudiciary.com, latestlaws.com) since the official site blocks automated fetches.

title: Sale of Immovable Property Defined
legal_text: Sale is a transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid, promised, or partly paid and partly promised. For tangible immovable property worth Rs. 100 or more, and for any transfer of an intangible property interest, a sale can only be made through a registered instrument. For tangible immovable property worth less than Rs. 100, sale may be made either by a registered instrument or simply by delivery of possession.
simple_explanation: Defines what a 'sale' of property legally is, and says that for anything but trivially low-value property, ownership can only be transferred through a registered sale deed — not just by handing over the property or signing an unregistered agreement.
purpose: Ensures certainty of title and a documented, verifiable record of property ownership transfers, reducing fraud and disputes.
punishment: Not a penal provision — an unregistered document purporting to sell property worth Rs. 100 or more does not transfer ownership and generally cannot be used as evidence of title in court.
relevant_documents: Registered sale deed, title documents/chain of ownership, payment proof, encumbrance certificate.
key_elements:
Transfer of ownership (not merely possession) in exchange for a price.
Price is paid, promised, or part-paid and part-promised.
A registered instrument is mandatory for property valued Rs. 100 or more.
An 'agreement to sell' is distinct from a completed sale and does not by itself transfer ownership.
relevant_information:
Whether the sale deed is actually registered at the Sub-Registrar's office, not merely notarized.
The seller's title chain and whether the registered document correctly describes the property and price.
Whether what you have is only an 'agreement to sell', not a registered sale deed.
keywords: sale deed, property sale, transfer of ownership, agreement to sell, section 54, transfer of property act
source: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Section 54. Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org and the ipleaders.in explainer.

title: Documents Requiring Compulsory Registration
legal_text: Compulsory registration applies to gift deeds of immovable property; non-testamentary documents worth Rs. 100 or more that create, declare, assign, limit, or extinguish any right, title, or interest in immovable property; leases from year to year, exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent; and certain non-testamentary decrees or orders affecting such rights. Since a 2001 amendment, documents recording a contract to transfer immovable property for consideration are also covered for specific-performance purposes.
simple_explanation: Lists which property-related documents must legally be registered with the Sub-Registrar to be valid — including sale deeds, gift deeds, and leases longer than a year.
purpose: Creates a reliable public record of property transactions, preventing fraud and title disputes.
punishment: Not a penal provision — an unregistered document that was required to be registered cannot affect the property and generally cannot be used as evidence of the transaction in court.
relevant_documents: Registered deed copy, index-II extract from the Sub-Registrar, encumbrance certificate.
key_elements:
Gift deeds of immovable property.
Non-testamentary documents worth Rs. 100+ affecting rights/title/interest in immovable property.
Leases from year to year, exceeding one year, or reserving yearly rent.
Certain contracts for transfer of immovable property (added by a 2001 amendment).
relevant_information:
Whether your sale/gift/lease deed is actually registered, with an entry in the Sub-Registrar's index.
The registration date and index-II entry, especially before purchasing property.
That an unregistered agreement may still matter for a specific-performance claim, but not for proving title.
keywords: document registration, sub-registrar, registration act, section 17, sale deed registration, lease registration
source: Registration Act, 1908, Section 17 (including the sub-section (1A) added by the 2001 amendment). Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org and legalserviceindia.com.

law_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title: Complaint of Sexual Harassment
legal_text: An aggrieved woman may submit a written complaint of workplace sexual harassment to the Internal Committee (or the Local Committee, if no Internal Committee exists) within three months of the incident, or the last incident in a series. If she is unable to write the complaint herself, a Committee member or officer must render reasonable assistance. The Committee may extend this deadline by up to three further months, for recorded reasons, where circumstances prevented timely filing.
simple_explanation: Lets a woman file a written complaint about workplace sexual harassment with her employer's Internal Committee (or a Local Committee if the workplace has none) within three months of the incident, extendable by up to three more months for good reason.
purpose: Gives women a confidential, accessible first channel to report workplace harassment without immediately going to police or court.
punishment: Not a penal provision itself — it governs how and when a complaint is filed; the harassment itself may separately be an offence under criminal law, and an employer's failure to constitute a required Committee is penalized under a different section of this Act.
relevant_documents: Written complaint to the Internal/Local Committee, any evidence of the incident (messages, emails, witness accounts).
key_elements:
Complainant must be a woman facing workplace sexual harassment.
Complaint must be in writing, with assistance available if needed.
Must be filed within 3 months of the incident, or last incident in a series.
Extendable by the Committee for up to 3 further months for recorded reasons.
relevant_information:
Exact date(s) of the incident(s) — the time limit is strict.
Whether the workplace has a constituted Internal Committee, or whether the complaint should go to the district Local Committee instead.
Written assistance from a Committee member is a right if you cannot write the complaint yourself.
keywords: posh act, workplace harassment, sexual harassment complaint, internal committee, section 9, icc complaint
source: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, Section 9. Cross-verified against the bare act text (kanoongpt.in) and ssrana.in.

title: Penalty for Giving or Taking Dowry
legal_text: Whoever gives, takes, or abets the giving or taking of dowry shall be punished with imprisonment of not less than five years, and with a fine of not less than fifteen thousand rupees or the value of the dowry, whichever is higher. A court may impose a lesser term of imprisonment only for adequate and special reasons recorded in its judgment. Genuinely voluntary, non-excessive customary wedding gifts given without any demand are exempt, provided they are entered in a list as prescribed.
simple_explanation: Makes it a crime to give, take, or help arrange dowry in connection with a marriage — covering the giver, the taker, and anyone who helps arrange it, with a minimum five-year jail term.
purpose: Criminalizes the dowry system, which drives dowry-related harassment, abuse, and financial exploitation of brides' families.
punishment: Imprisonment of not less than 5 years (reducible only for recorded special reasons), and a fine of not less than Rs. 15,000 or the dowry's value, whichever is greater.
relevant_documents: Written record of the dowry demand, wedding gift list (if any), police complaint, any related cruelty/dowry-death FIR.
key_elements:
Dowry (as defined by the Act) was given, taken, or demanded in connection with a marriage.
Applies equally to the person giving, the person taking, and anyone abetting.
A genuinely voluntary, listed customary gift given without any demand is exempt.
relevant_information:
Any written or recorded evidence of a dowry demand (messages, lists, witness accounts).
Whether related complaints exist under cruelty/dowry-death provisions of criminal law, since these often run alongside a Section 3 complaint.
The 1986 amendment's five-year minimum is the current governing penalty — older sources citing a six-month term are outdated.
keywords: dowry, dowry prohibition act, dowry demand, dowry harassment, section 3, giving taking dowry
source: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, Section 3 (as amended by the Dowry Prohibition (Amendment) Act, 1986). Cross-verified against indiankanoon.org, indiacode.nic.in, and casemine.com.

law_name: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Punishment for Penetrative Sexual Assault
legal_text: Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault on a child shall be punished with imprisonment of not less than ten years, extendable to imprisonment for life, and a fine. If the child is below sixteen years of age, the minimum term is twenty years, extendable to imprisonment for the remainder of the offender's natural life, and a fine. Fine amounts must be just and reasonable, and are payable to the victim for medical treatment and rehabilitation.
simple_explanation: Punishes penetrative sexual assault against a child (under 18) with a minimum of 10 years' imprisonment, rising to a minimum of 20 years if the child is under 16 — these minimums were raised by a 2019 amendment.
purpose: Deters and severely punishes penetrative sexual abuse of children, reflecting the 2019 amendment's tightening of minimum sentences.
punishment: Minimum 10 years' imprisonment, extendable to life, and fine; if the victim is under 16, minimum 20 years, extendable to imprisonment for the remainder of the offender's natural life, and fine.
relevant_documents: FIR / complaint to SJPU or police, medical examination report, Child Welfare Committee records.
key_elements:
Act meets the statutory definition of 'penetrative sexual assault'.
Victim is a 'child' — under 18 years of age under this Act.
Victim's exact age (under/over 16) determines which minimum sentence applies.
relevant_information:
Report to the local police or Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) — reporting is mandatory for anyone aware of the offence.
POCSO cases are tried in a designated Special Court with child-friendly, in-camera procedures.
This section is distinct from 'aggravated' penetrative sexual assault (a separate, more severe section) — do not confuse the two.
keywords: pocso, child sexual assault, child abuse law, penetrative sexual assault, section 4, child protection
source: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, as amended by the POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019. Cross-verified against advocategandhi.com, prsindia.org, and apnilaw.com.

law_name: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
title: Mandatory Reporting of Child Sexual Abuse
legal_text: Any person who has knowledge or reasonable apprehension that an offence under this Act has occurred, including the child concerned, must inform the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police. Reports must be recorded in writing, given an entry number, and read back to the informant. Failure to report or record such information is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both; a person in charge of a company or institution who fails to report an offence by a subordinate faces up to one year's imprisonment and a fine. Children are exempt from this penalty.
simple_explanation: Makes it a legal duty for anyone who knows or suspects a child sexual offence has happened to report it to the police or SJPU — and failing to do so is itself punishable, with a harsher penalty for institutional heads who fail to report a subordinate's offence.
purpose: Overcomes silence and institutional inaction around child sexual abuse by making reporting a duty for everyone, not just the victim or family.
punishment: Failure to report or record: up to 6 months' imprisonment, or fine, or both. An institutional head failing to report a subordinate's offence: up to 1 year's imprisonment and fine. Children are exempt from this penalty.
relevant_documents: Written report to SJPU/police with entry number, Child Welfare Committee referral record.
key_elements:
Reporter had actual knowledge or reasonable apprehension of an offence.
Failure was to report to the SJPU or police — not merely to a superior.
For the higher penalty, the accused must be an institutional head with a subordinate who committed the offence.
Genuine, good-faith reports carry civil and criminal immunity for the informant.
relevant_information:
A report can be made without your identity being made public.
Police must forward the report to the Child Welfare Committee or Special Court within 24 hours.
False or malicious complaints are separately punishable under a different section — this reporting duty only concerns genuine suspicion.
keywords: pocso reporting, mandatory reporting child abuse, section 19, section 21, failure to report, child protection
source: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, as amended by the POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019. Cross-verified against advocategandhi.com, prsindia.org, and apnilaw.com.

title: Right to Payment of Maternity Benefit
legal_text: Every woman is entitled to, and her employer is liable for, payment of maternity benefit at the rate of her average daily wage for the period of her actual absence — 26 weeks for a woman with fewer than two surviving children (of which not more than 8 weeks may be taken before the expected delivery date), and 12 weeks for a woman with two or more surviving children. Eligibility requires having worked for the employer for at least 80 days in the 12 months before the expected delivery date.
simple_explanation: Gives a working woman the right to paid maternity leave — 26 weeks if she has fewer than two surviving children, or 12 weeks otherwise — provided she has worked at least 80 days in the preceding year. This is the direct successor to the old Maternity Benefit Act, folded into the new labour codes that took effect in November 2025.
purpose: Protects women's health and income security around childbirth and discourages workplace discrimination against pregnant employees.
punishment: Not a penal provision for the woman — an employer who denies this benefit is liable for prosecution/penalty under the Code, and the benefit can be claimed via labour authorities or courts.
relevant_documents: Employment records, medical certificate confirming pregnancy/expected delivery date, written maternity benefit claim to the employer.
key_elements:
Worked at least 80 days for the employer in the 12 months before the expected delivery date.
Employer covered by the Code on Social Security.
Leave duration depends on the number of surviving children (26 weeks or 12 weeks).
Dismissal during maternity leave is generally barred.
relevant_information:
Proof of continuous employment and expected delivery date (doctor's certificate).
Employer's establishment size and whether it is covered under the Code.
Some state-level procedural rules under the new labour codes were still being finalized through 2026, which may affect enforcement details in a given state.
keywords: maternity leave, maternity benefit, pregnancy workplace rights, 26 weeks leave, code on social security, section 60
source: Code on Social Security, 2020, Section 60 — in force nationwide from 21 November 2025, replacing the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961. Cross-verified against the bare Code text (kanoongpt.in), with the specific 26/12-week durations corroborated by consistent independent secondary sources since the exact sub-clause was not directly fetchable.

title: Conditions Precedent to Retrenchment of Workers
legal_text: A worker who has been in continuous service for at least one year cannot be retrenched until given one month's written notice (or wages in lieu of notice), paid compensation equivalent to fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service (or any part exceeding six months), and until notice is served on the appropriate Government or authority.
simple_explanation: Before an employer can retrench (lay off) a worker with at least a year of continuous service, it must give one month's notice or pay in lieu, pay retrenchment compensation of 15 days' average pay per completed year of service, and notify the government. This is the direct successor to the old Industrial Disputes Act's Section 25F, folded into the new labour codes that took effect in November 2025.
purpose: Prevents arbitrary job loss and cushions workers financially during involuntary termination unrelated to misconduct.
punishment: Not a penal provision defining a crime — but retrenchment carried out without meeting these conditions can be declared illegal/void, and the Industrial Tribunal may order reinstatement with back wages.
relevant_documents: Employment/service records, retrenchment notice, compensation payment proof, correspondence with labour authorities.
key_elements:
Worker has at least one year of continuous service.
One month's written notice or pay in lieu of notice was given.
Retrenchment compensation (15 days' average pay per completed year) was actually paid.
Notice was served on the appropriate Government or authority.
relevant_information:
Length of continuous service with the employer.
Whether notice and compensation were actually paid, and when.
Whether the organization's size triggers additional government-permission requirements for larger establishments.
keywords: retrenchment, layoff, termination, industrial relations code, section 70, notice pay, compensation
source: Industrial Relations Code, 2020, Section 70 — in force nationwide from 21 November 2025, replacing Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. Cross-verified directly against the bare Code text on indiankanoon.org.

title: Equality Before Law
legal_text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
simple_explanation: The government cannot deny any person — citizen, foreign national, or company — either 'equality before the law' or 'the equal protection of the laws.' In practice: no one, including the State itself, is above the law; and people who are truly alike in similar situations must be treated alike, though the State may treat genuinely different groups differently if the distinction is real and logically connected to the law's purpose. Courts have also held that arbitrary government action by itself can violate this article, even without needing to show unequal treatment between two people.
purpose: Guarantees that everyone within India's territory is equally subject to the law and entitled to equal treatment under it, and forbids arbitrary state action.
punishment: Not a penal provision — remedies are constitutional, via a writ petition under Article 32 (Supreme Court) or Article 226 (High Court).
relevant_documents: Writ petition, evidence of the differential or arbitrary treatment.
key_elements:
Applies to any person within India's territory — citizens, non-citizens, and companies alike.
Equality before law: no one, including the State, is above the ordinary law.
Equal protection of the laws: equals must be treated alike, but the State may classify people differently if the classification has an intelligible differentia with a rational nexus to the law's object (the 'reasonable classification' test).
Arbitrary or unreasonable state action can itself be struck down under this article, independent of any comparison to another group.
relevant_information:
Whether the classification or rule being challenged has a real, sensible basis connected to its stated purpose.
Whether the state action was arbitrary or lacked any rational justification.
Whether a more specific right (e.g. Articles 15 or 16, which bar discrimination on specific grounds) applies more directly to the situation.
keywords: equality, article 14, equal protection, reasonable classification, arbitrary state action, discrimination, constitution
source: The Constitution of India, Article 14. Official text at indiacode.nic.in / legislative.gov.in blocks automated fetches; verbatim wording cross-verified identically across indiankanoon.org, constitutionofindia.net, drishtijudiciary.com, and lawbhoomi.com.
simple_explanation_te: పౌరుడు, విదేశీ పౌరుడు లేదా కంపెనీ అయినా — ఏ వ్యక్తికైనా ప్రభుత్వం 'చట్టం ముందు సమానత్వం' లేదా 'చట్టాల సమాన రక్షణ'ను నిరాకరించకూడదు. ఆచరణలో దీని అర్థం: ప్రభుత్వంతో సహా ఎవరూ చట్టానికి అతీతులు కారు; మరియు ఒకే విధమైన పరిస్థితుల్లో నిజంగా సమానమైన వ్యక్తులను సమానంగా చూడాలి, అయితే నిజమైన వ్యత్యాసం చట్టం యొక్క ఉద్దేశ్యానికి తార్కికంగా అనుసంధానించబడి ఉంటే వేర్వేరు వర్గాలను ప్రభుత్వం వేర్వేరుగా చూడవచ్చు. ఏకపక్ష ప్రభుత్వ చర్య, ఇద్దరు వ్యక్తుల మధ్య అసమాన ప్రవర్తనను చూపించాల్సిన అవసరం లేకుండానే, ఈ ఆర్టికల్‌ను ఉల్లంఘించవచ్చని కూడా న్యాయస్థానాలు తీర్పు ఇచ్చాయి.
purpose_te: భారతదేశ భూభాగంలో ఉన్న ప్రతి ఒక్కరూ చట్టానికి సమానంగా లోబడి ఉండాలని మరియు దాని కింద సమాన ప్రవర్తనకు అర్హులని హామీ ఇస్తుంది, మరియు ఏకపక్ష రాజ్య చర్యను నిషేధిస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — పరిష్కారాలు రాజ్యాంగపరమైనవి, ఆర్టికల్ 32 (సుప్రీంకోర్టు) లేదా ఆర్టికల్ 226 (హైకోర్టు) కింద రిట్ పిటిషన్ ద్వారా.
key_elements_te:
భారతదేశ భూభాగంలో ఉన్న ఏ వ్యక్తికైనా వర్తిస్తుంది — పౌరులు, పౌరులు కానివారు మరియు కంపెనీలు అందరికీ సమానంగా.
చట్టం ముందు సమానత్వం: ప్రభుత్వంతో సహా ఎవరూ సాధారణ చట్టానికి అతీతులు కారు.
చట్టాల సమాన రక్షణ: సమానులను సమానంగా చూడాలి, కానీ వర్గీకరణకు స్పష్టమైన ప్రాతిపదిక మరియు చట్టం లక్ష్యానికి తార్కిక సంబంధం ఉంటే ప్రభుత్వం వేర్వేరు వర్గాలను వేర్వేరుగా వర్గీకరించవచ్చు ('సహేతుక వర్గీకరణ' పరీక్ష).
ఏకపక్ష లేదా అసమంజసమైన రాజ్య చర్యను, మరొక సమూహంతో పోల్చకుండానే, ఈ ఆర్టికల్ కింద కొట్టివేయవచ్చు.
relevant_information_te:
సవాలు చేయబడుతున్న వర్గీకరణ లేదా నియమానికి దాని ప్రకటిత ఉద్దేశ్యానికి సంబంధించిన నిజమైన, సహేతుకమైన ప్రాతిపదిక ఉందా.
రాజ్య చర్య ఏకపక్షంగా ఉందా లేదా హేతుబద్ధమైన సమర్థన లేకుండా ఉందా.
ఈ పరిస్థితికి మరింత నేరుగా వర్తించే మరింత నిర్దిష్టమైన హక్కు (ఉదా. ఆర్టికల్ 15 లేదా 16) ఉందా.
relevant_documents_te: రిట్ పిటిషన్, వ్యత్యాసమైన లేదా ఏకపక్ష ప్రవర్తనకు సంబంధించిన ఆధారాలు.

title: Mortgage of Immovable Property Defined
legal_text: A mortgage is the transfer of an interest in specific immoveable property for the purpose of securing the payment of money advanced or to be advanced by way of loan, an existing or future debt, or the performance of an engagement which may give rise to a pecuniary liability.
simple_explanation: When you take a loan against property (like a home loan), the lender doesn't just rely on your promise to repay — it takes a legal interest in the property as security, called a mortgage. You are the 'mortgagor' and the lender is the 'mortgagee.' Depending on how it's structured, this can be done through a registered mortgage deed, or — commonly for housing finance — simply by handing over the property's original title deeds to the lender (an 'equitable mortgage'), which unusually needs no separate written, registered document.
purpose: Establishes the legal framework for using immovable property as security for a loan or debt, and defines the rights of mortgagors and mortgagees.
punishment: Not a penal provision — governs civil rights between mortgagor and mortgagee; on default, the mortgagee's remedy is a civil suit for sale or foreclosure (Section 67), not a criminal penalty.
relevant_documents: Registered mortgage deed (or the original title deeds, for a deposit-of-title-deeds mortgage), loan agreement, encumbrance certificate.
key_elements:
Six recognized kinds of mortgage: simple mortgage, mortgage by conditional sale, usufructuary mortgage, English mortgage, mortgage by deposit of title-deeds, and anomalous mortgage (Section 58(b)-(g)).
A mortgage (other than by deposit of title-deeds) securing Rs. 100 or more must be made by a registered instrument, signed by the mortgagor and attested by at least two witnesses (Section 59).
A mortgage by deposit of title-deeds needs no written or registered instrument — simply handing over the property's title deeds with intent to create security is enough.
On default, whether the mortgagee can sue for sale, foreclosure, or both depends on which kind of mortgage was created (Section 67).
relevant_information:
Whether your mortgage is actually a registered instrument at the Sub-Registrar's office, not just a private or notarized agreement.
Which of the six kinds of mortgage applies to your loan, since it directly affects the lender's rights if you default.
Whether the transaction is genuinely a mortgage or actually a conditional sale of the property — the two are distinguished by whether the underlying debt still exists.
keywords: mortgage, home loan, property security, mortgagor, mortgagee, equitable mortgage, title deeds, section 58, transfer of property act

simple_explanation_te: మీరు ఆస్తిపై రుణం తీసుకున్నప్పుడు (గృహ రుణం వంటివి), రుణదాత మీ తిరిగి చెల్లిస్తానన్న వాగ్దానంపై మాత్రమే ఆధారపడడు — అతను ఆస్తిపై చట్టపరమైన హక్కును భద్రతగా తీసుకుంటాడు, దీన్ని తనఖా అంటారు. మీరు 'తనఖాదారు' (మార్ట్‌గేజర్), రుణదాత 'తనఖా గ్రహీత' (మార్ట్‌గేజీ). దీన్ని రిజిస్టర్డ్ తనఖా దస్తావేజు ద్వారా చేయవచ్చు, లేదా — గృహ రుణాల విషయంలో సాధారణంగా — ఆస్తి యొక్క అసలు టైటిల్ డీడ్‌లను రుణదాతకు అప్పగించడం ద్వారా చేయవచ్చు ('ఈక్విటబుల్ మార్ట్‌గేజ్'), దీనికి వేరుగా వ్రాతపూర్వక, రిజిస్టర్డ్ పత్రం అవసరం లేదు.
purpose_te: రుణం లేదా అప్పుకు భద్రతగా స్థిరాస్తిని ఉపయోగించడానికి చట్టపరమైన చట్రాన్ని ఏర్పరుస్తుంది, మరియు తనఖాదారులు మరియు తనఖా గ్రహీతల హక్కులను నిర్వచిస్తుంది.
punishment_te: ఇది శిక్షార్హమైన నిబంధన కాదు — తనఖాదారు మరియు తనఖా గ్రహీత మధ్య పౌర హక్కులను నియంత్రిస్తుంది; డిఫాల్ట్ అయినప్పుడు, తనఖా గ్రహీత పరిష్కారం విక్రయం లేదా ఫోర్‌క్లోజర్ కోసం పౌర దావా (సెక్షన్ 67), క్రిమినల్ శిక్ష కాదు.
key_elements_te:
ఆరు రకాల తనఖాలు గుర్తించబడ్డాయి: సాధారణ తనఖా, షరతులతో కూడిన అమ్మకం ద్వారా తనఖా, యూసుఫ్రక్చురీ తనఖా, ఇంగ్లీష్ తనఖా, టైటిల్ డీడ్‌ల డిపాజిట్ ద్వారా తనఖా, మరియు అసాధారణ తనఖా (సెక్షన్ 58(b)-(g)).
రూ. 100 లేదా అంతకంటే ఎక్కువ మొత్తానికి భద్రత కల్పించే తనఖా (టైటిల్ డీడ్‌ల డిపాజిట్ మినహా) తనఖాదారు సంతకం చేసి, కనీసం ఇద్దరు సాక్షుల సమక్షంలో రిజిస్టర్డ్ పత్రం ద్వారా చేయాలి (సెక్షన్ 59).
టైటిల్ డీడ్‌ల డిపాజిట్ ద్వారా తనఖాకు వ్రాతపూర్వక లేదా రిజిస్టర్డ్ పత్రం అవసరం లేదు — భద్రత కల్పించే ఉద్దేశంతో టైటిల్ డీడ్‌లను అప్పగించడమే సరిపోతుంది.
డిఫాల్ట్ అయినప్పుడు, తనఖా గ్రహీత విక్రయం, ఫోర్‌క్లోజర్, లేదా రెండింటికీ దావా వేయగలరా అనేది సృష్టించిన తనఖా రకంపై ఆధారపడి ఉంటుంది (సెక్షన్ 67).
relevant_information_te:
మీ తనఖా నిజంగా సబ్-రిజిస్ట్రార్ కార్యాలయంలో రిజిస్టర్డ్ పత్రమేనా, కేవలం ప్రైవేట్ లేదా నోటరైజ్డ్ ఒప్పందం కాదా.
మీ రుణానికి ఆరు రకాల తనఖాలలో ఏది వర్తిస్తుంది, ఎందుకంటే మీరు డిఫాల్ట్ అయితే రుణదాత హక్కులపై దీని ప్రత్యక్ష ప్రభావం ఉంటుంది.
లావాదేవీ నిజంగా తనఖానా లేదా వాస్తవానికి ఆస్తి యొక్క షరతులతో కూడిన అమ్మకం — అసలు అప్పు ఇంకా ఉందా లేదా అనే దాని ఆధారంగా ఈ రెండింటినీ వేరు చేస్తారు.
relevant_documents_te: రిజిస్టర్డ్ తనఖా దస్తావేజు (లేదా టైటిల్ డీడ్‌ల డిపాజిట్ తనఖా అయితే అసలు టైటిల్ డీడ్‌లు), రుణ ఒప్పందం, ఎన్‌కంబరెన్స్ సర్టిఫికేట్.
